fields.what_passage_says: Making alterations costs $40 per person per year compared to a $6,500 gain in employee productivity.
fields.why_answer: The comparison of costs versus huge productivity returns represents the financial benefits (heading viii: 'The financial benefits of efficient workplaces').
fields.paraphrase: $40 cost vs $6,500 increase in productivity -> financial benefits of efficient workplaces
fields.tip: Dollar amounts and economic comparisons point to financial benefits.

fields.question_text: Section C
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has six paragraphs, A-F. Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below. Write the correct number, i-viii.
fields.explanation: Coming to a research laboratory means they were assessed outside their usual workplace (heading vi: 'Workers were assessed outside of their usual workplace').
fields.passage_excerpt: For six days over two weeks, 24 office workers with administrative, technical, professional or managerial jobs came to the lab and performed their regular work under minimal supervision, as well as participating in an hour and a half of cognitive testing at the end of the day.
fields.what_question_asks: Which heading describes the methodology in paragraph C.
fields.what_passage_says: Office workers 'came to the lab and performed their regular work' and cognitive testing there.
fields.why_answer: Coming to a research laboratory means they were assessed outside their usual workplace (heading vi: 'Workers were assessed outside of their usual workplace').
fields.paraphrase: came to the lab -> assessed outside of their usual workplace
fields.tip: Distinguish between the laboratory simulation in C and the real-world buildings in D.

fields.question_text: Section D
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has six paragraphs, A-F. Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below. Write the correct number, i-viii.
fields.explanation: Heading iii, 'The assessment of workplaces in several locations', matches the paragraph's description of testing multiple buildings across five different cities.
fields.passage_excerpt: Using the same methodology, they compared test scores of 109 people working in 10 buildings - about 12 people per site - in two buildings in each of five cities.
fields.what_question_asks: The question asks which heading best summarises paragraph D's main topic.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph D describes testing '109 people working in 10 buildings ... in two buildings in each of five cities' — meaning the study expanded to compare multiple real workplaces across different cities.
fields.why_answer: Heading iii, 'The assessment of workplaces in several locations', matches the paragraph's description of testing multiple buildings across five different cities.
fields.paraphrase: question: 'the assessment of workplaces in several locations' → passage: '10 buildings ... in two buildings in each of five cities'
fields.tip: The mention of 'five cities' and multiple buildings is a strong signal pointing to a heading about several locations.

fields.question_text: Section E
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has six paragraphs, A-F. Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below. Write the correct number, i-viii.
fields.explanation: This case study examines the effects of a new green building on staff, matching heading i ('The effects of a new environmentally friendly building on the people who work there').
fields.passage_excerpt: A recently constructed building on the Washington University campus in St. Louis, US, is providing another opportunity to examine how green building design can affect health and behavior.
fields.what_question_asks: Which heading summarizes the investigation in paragraph E.
fields.what_passage_says: Hillman Hall, a green building designed with high environmental standards, was studied before and after occupancy to measure impacts on health, collaboration, and physical activity.
fields.why_answer: This case study examines the effects of a new green building on staff, matching heading i ('The effects of a new environmentally friendly building on the people who work there').
fields.paraphrase: green building design affect health and behavior -> effects of a new environmentally friendly building on people
fields.tip: 'Green building' equals 'environmentally friendly building'.

fields.question_text: Section F
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has six paragraphs, A-F. Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below. Write the correct number, i-viii.
fields.explanation: Working across diverse professions represents involving a range of specialists (heading v: 'Achieving design efficiency by involving a range of specialists').
fields.passage_excerpt: Like other researchers in this growing field, Eyler sees multidisciplinary collaboration as the key to success. Administrators, public health faculty and architects worked together to create a building
fields.what_question_asks: Which heading captures the main theme of paragraph F.
fields.what_passage_says: Eyler emphasizes 'multidisciplinary collaboration', bringing together administrators, public health faculty, and architects.
fields.why_answer: Working across diverse professions represents involving a range of specialists (heading v: 'Achieving design efficiency by involving a range of specialists').
fields.paraphrase: multidisciplinary collaboration ... teams with varied backgrounds -> involving a range of specialists
fields.tip: 'Multidisciplinary' means involving varied specialists.

fields.question_text: Further investigations will result in improved wellbeing and efficiency.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 20-23) and the list of researchers below. Match each statement with the correct researcher, A-D.
fields.explanation: 'Promoting better health and performance' equates to improved wellbeing and efficiency, stated by Craig Zimring.
fields.passage_excerpt: If these findings are replicated in other labs and in real-world work environments,' he says, 'they could lead to designs that provide much more outside air through mechanical ventilation or operable windows, for example' - in turn, promoting better health and performance.
fields.what_question_asks: Which researcher noted that replicating research will yield better health and work performance.
fields.what_passage_says: Craig Zimring notes that if findings are replicated, they could lead to designs 'promoting better health and performance'.
fields.why_answer: 'Promoting better health and performance' equates to improved wellbeing and efficiency, stated by Craig Zimring.
fields.paraphrase: improved wellbeing and efficiency -> promoting better health and performance
fields.tip: Match 'replicated' with 'further investigations'.

fields.question_text: A person's opinion of their workspace may influence how well they perform at work.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 20-23) and the list of researchers below. Match each statement with the correct researcher, A-D.
fields.explanation: 'How someone feels about their working environment' matches 'a person's opinion of their workspace', attributed to MacNaughton.
fields.passage_excerpt: This has led researchers to believe that other factors, such as how someone feels about their working environment, may also play a part, notes Harvard research fellow Piers MacNaughton, who led the study.
fields.what_question_asks: Which researcher suggested that workers' personal feelings about their environment affect cognitive results.
fields.what_passage_says: Piers MacNaughton notes that 'how someone feels about their working environment, may also play a part' in differing cognitive function scores.
fields.why_answer: 'How someone feels about their working environment' matches 'a person's opinion of their workspace', attributed to MacNaughton.
fields.paraphrase: person's opinion -> how someone feels about their working environment
fields.tip: Look for MacNaughton's name in paragraph D.

fields.question_text: The design of a workplace can have an impact on how much staff work with their colleagues.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 20-23) and the list of researchers below. Match each statement with the correct researcher, A-D.
fields.explanation: 'Spontaneous collaborations' means working with colleagues, investigated and reported by Amy Eyler.
fields.passage_excerpt: Results showed that people were more likely to take part in spontaneous collaborations in the new space than in the older ones, and to be physically active.
fields.what_question_asks: Which researcher observed that workspace design alters teamwork and collaboration frequency.
fields.what_passage_says: Amy Eyler found that in the newly designed space, staff were 'more likely to take part in spontaneous collaborations'.
fields.why_answer: 'Spontaneous collaborations' means working with colleagues, investigated and reported by Amy Eyler.
fields.paraphrase: work with their colleagues -> spontaneous collaborations
fields.tip: Eyler studied collaboration at Hillman Hall in paragraph E.

fields.question_text: A worker's mental capacity may be considerably reduced due to their working environment.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 20-23) and the list of researchers below. Match each statement with the correct researcher, A-D.
fields.explanation: 'Significantly lower cognitive performance' matches 'mental capacity may be considerably reduced', quoted from Zimring.
fields.passage_excerpt: The findings are remarkable for showing in a well-controlled study, that indoor air quality can significantly lower cognitive performance in buildings that would otherwise meet current building standards, notes environmental psychologist Craig Zimring
fields.what_question_asks: Which researcher highlighted that indoor environmental conditions can significantly depress cognitive performance.
fields.what_passage_says: Craig Zimring notes findings show indoor air quality can 'significantly lower cognitive performance'.
fields.why_answer: 'Significantly lower cognitive performance' matches 'mental capacity may be considerably reduced', quoted from Zimring.
fields.paraphrase: mental capacity considerably reduced -> significantly lower cognitive performance
fields.tip: 'Cognitive performance' refers to mental capacity.

fields.question_text: Allen's first study was done at the Syracuse Center, which focuses on researching ___
fields.question_instructions: Complete the summary below. Write ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
fields.explanation: 'Sustainability' is the field the organization focuses on.
fields.passage_excerpt: The team's first study, published in Environmental Health Perspectives, was conducted at the Syracuse Center of Excellence, a US research organization devoted to studying and developing sustainability.
fields.what_question_asks: What field or subject the Syracuse Center of Excellence is devoted to researching.
fields.what_passage_says: The Syracuse Center is 'devoted to studying and developing sustainability'.
fields.why_answer: 'Sustainability' is the field the organization focuses on.
fields.paraphrase: focuses on researching -> devoted to studying and developing sustainability
fields.tip: 'Devoted to studying' matches 'focuses on researching'.

fields.question_text: All staff carried out normal duties during the day without much ___
fields.question_instructions: Complete the summary below. Write ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
fields.explanation: 'Minimal supervision' matches 'without much supervision'.
fields.passage_excerpt: For six days over two weeks, 24 office workers with administrative, technical, professional or managerial jobs came to the lab and performed their regular work under minimal supervision, as well as participating in an hour and a half of cognitive testing at the end of the day.
fields.what_question_asks: Under what condition workers performed their regular duties during the study.
fields.what_passage_says: They performed regular work 'under minimal supervision'.
fields.why_answer: 'Minimal supervision' matches 'without much supervision'.
fields.paraphrase: without much ___ -> under minimal supervision
fields.tip: 'Minimal' means without much.

fields.question_text: Later in the day participants were assessed as they performed tasks which required them to play a role, for example acting as ___ while dealing with practical problems.
fields.question_instructions: Complete the summary below. Write ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
fields.explanation: 'Mayor' is the exact role participants acted as.
fields.passage_excerpt: The cognitive tasks used in the study had participants respond to online scenarios that mimic real-life situations, such as running a city as a mayor.
fields.what_question_asks: What municipal role participants simulated during the cognitive tasks.
fields.what_passage_says: Scenarios had participants 'running a city as a mayor'.
fields.why_answer: 'Mayor' is the exact role participants acted as.
fields.paraphrase: acting as ___ -> running a city as a mayor
fields.tip: Look for 'acting as' or 'running a city as' in paragraph C.

fields.question_text: economic evidence for play in medieval England
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 3 has eight paragraphs, A-H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-H.
fields.explanation: Commercial manufacture, buying toys, and taxation represent economic evidence (Paragraph D).
fields.passage_excerpt: Girls had dolls, known before the 17th century as 'poppets' or puppets, commercially manufactured, imported and, in 1582, taxed at a halfpenny each.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph presents financial or commercial proof regarding medieval play.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph D cites commercial manufacturing, imports, and doll taxation at a halfpenny in 1582, as well as an English toy industry by 1300.
fields.why_answer: Commercial manufacture, buying toys, and taxation represent economic evidence (Paragraph D).
fields.paraphrase: economic evidence -> commercially manufactured, imported and ... taxed at a halfpenny
fields.tip: Commercial manufacturing, prices, and taxes are hallmarks of economic evidence.

fields.question_text: an example of how children created their own toys
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 3 has eight paragraphs, A-H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-H.
fields.explanation: Building towns and castles from beach sand exemplifies children making their own play objects (Paragraph D).
fields.passage_excerpt: Gerald of Wales recalls how he and his brothers built towns, palaces, churches and monasteries from sand at Manorbier Castle in about 1150 (perhaps on the nearby beach).
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph gives an instance of children making their own play items instead of buying them.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph D describes Gerald of Wales and his brothers building towns and castles out of sand on the beach.
fields.why_answer: Building towns and castles from beach sand exemplifies children making their own play objects (Paragraph D).
fields.paraphrase: created their own toys -> built towns, palaces, churches and monasteries from sand
fields.tip: Sand constructions made by children demonstrate self-made play.

fields.question_text: an example of warlike play approved by grown-ups
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 3 has eight paragraphs, A-H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-H.
fields.explanation: Archery encouraged by adults to train boys for warrior roles matches warlike play approved by grown-ups (Paragraph E).
fields.passage_excerpt: Boys in the later Middle Ages shot arrows with bows and archery is an example of a sport encouraged by adults, who wanted boys to grow up to play their part in what was, for most men, a warrior society.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph mentions adult-endorsed military-style recreation.
fields.what_passage_says: Archery was encouraged by adults to train boys for roles in a warrior society.
fields.why_answer: Archery encouraged by adults to train boys for warrior roles matches warlike play approved by grown-ups (Paragraph E).
fields.paraphrase: warlike play approved by grown-ups -> archery is an example of a sport encouraged by adults ... for a warrior society
fields.tip: 'Encouraged by adults' matches 'approved by grown-ups'.

fields.question_text: a political event mirrored in children's play
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 3 has eight paragraphs, A-H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-H.
fields.explanation: Children crowning kings and fighting right after King Richard II was overthrown mirrors the political event (Paragraph F).
fields.passage_excerpt: In 1400, six months after King Richard II had been overthrown by Henry IV, the children of London gathered together and chose themselves kings.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph describes children imitating real-world governance or monarchical struggles.
fields.what_passage_says: Six months after King Richard II was overthrown, London children gathered, chose kings, and made war upon each other.
fields.why_answer: Children crowning kings and fighting right after King Richard II was overthrown mirrors the political event (Paragraph F).
fields.paraphrase: political event mirrored -> after King Richard II had been overthrown ... children gathered together and chose themselves kings
fields.tip: Overthrowing of a king is a major political event.

fields.question_text: the origin of an academic debate about medieval life
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 3 has eight paragraphs, A-H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-H.
fields.explanation: Ariès's publication in Centuries of Childhood originated the ongoing scholarly debate (Paragraph B).
fields.passage_excerpt: Forty years ago, the French historian Philippe Aries argued, in Centuries of Childhood, that childhood in the Middle Ages did not exist in its modern sense.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph introduces the foundational thesis that sparked historical controversy over childhood.
fields.what_passage_says: Philippe Ariès argued in Centuries of Childhood that medieval childhood did not exist, prompting subsequent historians to dispute his claim.
fields.why_answer: Ariès's publication in Centuries of Childhood originated the ongoing scholarly debate (Paragraph B).
fields.paraphrase: origin of an academic debate -> Philippe Aries argued ... More recent historians have disputed this
fields.tip: 'Historians have disputed' indicates an academic debate.

fields.question_instructions: Match each date (Questions 32-35) with the correct event, A-J.
fields.explanation: Option I, 'children's gang warfare', matches this description of children forming groups and fighting violently, dated to 1400.
fields.passage_excerpt: In 1400, six months after King Richard II had been overthrown by Henry IV, the children of London gathered together and chose themselves kings.
fields.what_question_asks: The question asks what event happened in the year 1400.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage describes children in London gathering and fighting each other 'in thousands', 'whereby many died' — a violent conflict among children's groups.
fields.why_answer: Option I, 'children's gang warfare', matches this description of children forming groups and fighting violently, dated to 1400.
fields.paraphrase: question: '1400' → passage: 'the children of London gathered together and chose themselves kings ... made war upon each other'
fields.tip: 'Made war upon each other' is a strong signal for 'gang warfare' among the children.

fields.question_instructions: Match each date (Questions 32-35) with the correct event, A-J.
fields.explanation: Cataloguing play in March, summer, and autumn is a description of seasonal activities (Option J).
fields.passage_excerpt: In 1518, the poet Alexander Barclay records children playing with tops in March, looking for fruit in summer and making footballs by filling pigs' bladders with dried peas in autumn.
fields.what_question_asks: What record is associated with the year 1518.
fields.what_passage_says: In 1518, Alexander Barclay recorded activities across spring, summer, and autumn.
fields.why_answer: Cataloguing play in March, summer, and autumn is a description of seasonal activities (Option J).
fields.paraphrase: 1518 -> March, summer, autumn -> seasonal activities
fields.tip: Months and seasons point directly to seasonal activities.

fields.question_instructions: Match each date (Questions 32-35) with the correct event, A-J.
fields.explanation: In 1582 dolls were taxed at a halfpenny each (Option F).
fields.passage_excerpt: Girls had dolls, known before the 17th century as 'poppets' or puppets, commercially manufactured, imported and, in 1582, taxed at a halfpenny each.
fields.what_question_asks: What took place in 1582.
fields.what_passage_says: Dolls (poppets) were 'in 1582, taxed at a halfpenny each'.
fields.why_answer: In 1582 dolls were taxed at a halfpenny each (Option F).
fields.paraphrase: 1582 -> taxed at a halfpenny each -> dolls taxed in England
fields.tip: Look for tax records and monetary amounts.

fields.question_instructions: Match each date (Questions 32-35) with the correct event, A-J.
fields.explanation: Vitai Lampada was a celebrated poem celebrating the value of games (Option C).
fields.passage_excerpt: The ringing chorus of Sir Henry Newbolt's celebrated cricket poem Vitai Lampada (1908) sums up views about play in 19th- and early 20th-century Britain.
fields.what_question_asks: What publication occurred in 1908.
fields.what_passage_says: Sir Henry Newbolt's cricket poem Vitai Lampada (1908) championed the social and disciplinary values of games.
fields.why_answer: Vitai Lampada was a celebrated poem celebrating the value of games (Option C).
fields.paraphrase: 1908 -> cricket poem Vitai Lampada ... sums up views about play -> poem about value of games
fields.tip: Newbolt's 1908 work is explicitly called a celebrated poem.

fields.question_text: Little is known about adult attitudes to children's play in the Middle Ages.
fields.question_instructions: Choose YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer, NO if it contradicts the claims, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
fields.explanation: Knowing 'much' and 'what their elders thought' directly contradicts 'little is known'. The answer is NO.
fields.passage_excerpt: The notion that children's play should be used for educational and social purposes goes back at least to the ancient Greeks and the toys and games of medieval England tell us much about how adults then saw childhood.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether modern historians lack information about medieval adult perspectives on play.
fields.what_passage_says: The text states that toys and games 'tell us much about how adults then saw childhood', and 'We know not only how medieval English children played but what their elders thought on the subject'.
fields.why_answer: Knowing 'much' and 'what their elders thought' directly contradicts 'little is known'. The answer is NO.
fields.paraphrase: question: 'little is known' contradicts passage: 'tell us much about how adults then saw childhood ... know what their elders thought'
fields.tip: 'Tell us much' is the direct opposite of 'little is known'.

fields.question_text: Most toys were imported into England before 1300.
fields.question_instructions: Choose YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer, NO if it contradicts the claims, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
fields.explanation: The claim about 'most toys' being imported before 1300 is not substantiated in the text.
fields.passage_excerpt: Indeed, by 1300 it appears there was a toy industry in England.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether imported toys made up the majority of English toys prior to 1300.
fields.what_passage_says: The text says there was a domestic toy industry in England by 1300 and mentions imported dolls, but never states what proportion of toys were imported before 1300.
fields.why_answer: The claim about 'most toys' being imported before 1300 is not substantiated in the text.
fields.paraphrase: No proportion like 'most toys' before 1300 is mentioned.
fields.tip: Watch for quantifiers like 'most' — if proportions are unstated, it is NOT GIVEN.

fields.question_text: Medieval children celebrated the seasons in their own ways.
fields.question_instructions: Choose YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer, NO if it contradicts the claims, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
fields.explanation: Having their own semi-detached observances agrees with celebrating seasons in their own ways (YES).
fields.passage_excerpt: Children shared in the adult round of religious festivals, but had their own observances as well, semi-detached from their elders.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether children held their own seasonal traditions distinct from adults.
fields.what_passage_says: Children 'had their own observances as well, semi-detached from their elders' regarding the seasonal cycle.
fields.why_answer: Having their own semi-detached observances agrees with celebrating seasons in their own ways (YES).
fields.paraphrase: celebrated the seasons in their own ways -> had their own observances as well, semi-detached from their elders
fields.tip: 'Own observances' equates to 'their own ways'.

fields.question_text: Medieval children made presents for their parents on special occasions.
fields.question_instructions: Choose YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer, NO if it contradicts the claims, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
fields.explanation: Children making presents for parents is entirely unmentioned in the text.
fields.passage_excerpt: We know, for example, that adults gave children toys from infancy onwards.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether children crafted gifts for their mothers and fathers during celebrations.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage mentions adults giving toys to children, but never mentions children making gifts for parents.
fields.why_answer: Children making presents for parents is entirely unmentioned in the text.
fields.paraphrase: No mention of children giving presents to parents.
fields.tip: Do not confuse adults giving toys to children with children giving gifts to adults.

fields.question_text: Parents and children in the Middle Ages behaved much as they do today.
fields.question_instructions: Choose YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer, NO if it contradicts the claims, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
fields.explanation: 'In major respects, a modern one' and 'always been much the same' confirms the statement as YES.
fields.passage_excerpt: We can answer Aries's thesis, then, with a resounding 'No!'. Childhood has always been much the same.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether the parent-child dynamic in medieval times resembled contemporary family life.
fields.what_passage_says: The author concludes that 'the relationship between adults and children in medieval society was, in major respects, a modern one' and 'Childhood has always been much the same'.
fields.why_answer: 'In major respects, a modern one' and 'always been much the same' confirms the statement as YES.
fields.paraphrase: behaved much as they do today -> relationship was, in major respects, a modern one ... has always been much the same
fields.tip: 'A modern one' confirms similarity to today.

fields.question_text: In Luapula Province, land has traditionally been given to people on the basis of ___
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentences below. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
fields.explanation: 'Need' is the exact word used in the passage to define how land was allocated.
fields.passage_excerpt: land in Luapula Province is not owned by individuals but, as in many other parts of Africa, is allocated by the headman or headwoman of a village to people of either sex according to need.
fields.what_question_asks: On what criteria or basis land was traditionally distributed to villagers in Luapula Province.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage says land is allocated by village leaders 'according to need'.
fields.why_answer: 'Need' is the exact word used in the passage to define how land was allocated.
fields.paraphrase: given to people on the basis of ___ -> allocated ... according to need
fields.tip: Look for synonyms: 'allocated' corresponds to 'given to people'.

fields.question_text: The citemene system involves planting crops in the ___ of wood.
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentences below. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
fields.explanation: 'Ashes' is the exact substance left from burned tree branches where crops are planted.
fields.passage_excerpt: Most of the traditional cropping in Luapula Province is based on citemene, a system whereby crops are grown on the ashes of tree branches.
fields.what_question_asks: What material from burned wood crops are planted into in the citemene system.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage explains that in the citemene system, 'crops are grown on the ashes of tree branches'.
fields.why_answer: 'Ashes' is the exact substance left from burned tree branches where crops are planted.
fields.paraphrase: planting crops in the ___ of wood -> crops are grown on the ashes of tree branches
fields.tip: Locate the definition of citemene in paragraph 2.

fields.question_text: In the citemene system, ___ is the last crop to be planted.
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentences below. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
fields.explanation: Because the sequence ends with cassava, it is the last crop to be planted.
fields.passage_excerpt: The diverse sequence ends with the vegetable cassava, which is often planted next to the last but one crop before this is harvested.
fields.what_question_asks: Which crop is planted at the final stage of the crop rotation sequence.
fields.what_passage_says: The text states: 'The diverse sequence ends with the vegetable cassava'.
fields.why_answer: Because the sequence ends with cassava, it is the last crop to be planted.
fields.paraphrase: last crop to be planted -> diverse sequence ends with the vegetable cassava
fields.tip: 'Sequence ends with' directly matches 'last crop'.

fields.question_text: In areas without trees, crops are planted in a ___
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentences below. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
fields.explanation: 'A series of ridges' (or 'series of ridges') is what is built and planted with crops.
fields.passage_excerpt: When forest is not available, a situation which is increasingly the case nowadays, a series of ridges is built, in which combinations of maize, beans, groundnuts and sweet potatoes are then planted
fields.what_question_asks: What physical ground structure is constructed for planting when there are no forests or trees.
fields.what_passage_says: When forest is unavailable, 'a series of ridges is built, in which combinations of maize, beans... are then planted'.
fields.why_answer: 'A series of ridges' (or 'series of ridges') is what is built and planted with crops.
fields.paraphrase: in areas without trees -> when forest is not available; crops are planted in a ___ -> in which ... are then planted
fields.tip: Write 'series of ridges' to fit the grammatical structure.

fields.question_text: If conditions are right, fruit trees may be planted near ___
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentences below. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
fields.explanation: 'Houses' is the location where fruit trees are planted.
fields.passage_excerpt: Where their roots have year-round access to water, mango, guava and oil-palm trees are often grown around houses, forming a traditional agro-forestry system
fields.what_question_asks: Near what buildings or structures fruit trees are cultivated when water is available year-round.
fields.what_passage_says: Where roots access water, fruit trees 'are often grown around houses'.
fields.why_answer: 'Houses' is the location where fruit trees are planted.
fields.paraphrase: planted near ___ -> grown around houses
fields.tip: 'Grown around' is a direct paraphrase of 'planted near'.

fields.question_text: They yield the biggest profits for farmers.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 6-9) and the list of animals below. Match each statement with the correct animal, A, B or C.
fields.explanation: 'Remunerative' means profitable, directly identifying fish (Option A) as yielding the biggest profits.
fields.passage_excerpt: Fishing has always been a far more remunerative activity in Luapula than crop husbandry. It provides a much needed protein supplement to the diet, as well as being the one substantial source of cash.
fields.what_question_asks: Which animal activity produces the largest financial return/profit for local people.
fields.what_passage_says: Fishing has always been 'far more remunerative' and 'the one substantial source of cash'.
fields.why_answer: 'Remunerative' means profitable, directly identifying fish (Option A) as yielding the biggest profits.
fields.paraphrase: yield the biggest profits -> far more remunerative activity ... one substantial source of cash
fields.tip: 'Remunerative' means lucrative or financially rewarding.

fields.question_text: They may be consumed on special occasions.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 6-9) and the list of animals below. Match each statement with the correct animal, A, B or C.
fields.explanation: Being slaughtered for ceremonies or important visitors matches consumed on special occasions, identifying Goats (Option B).
fields.passage_excerpt: most people keep freely roaming chickens and goats. These act as a reserve for bartering, but may also be occasionally slaughtered for ceremonies, or for entertaining important visitors.
fields.what_question_asks: Which animal is eaten during ceremonies or when hosting special guests.
fields.what_passage_says: Goats and chickens 'may also be occasionally slaughtered for ceremonies, or for entertaining important visitors'.
fields.why_answer: Being slaughtered for ceremonies or important visitors matches consumed on special occasions, identifying Goats (Option B).
fields.paraphrase: consumed on special occasions -> slaughtered for ceremonies, or for entertaining important visitors
fields.tip: 'Ceremonies' and 'entertaining important visitors' represent special occasions.

fields.question_text: Because of insect pests, they do not thrive.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 6-9) and the list of animals below. Match each statement with the correct animal, A, B or C.
fields.explanation: The tsetse fly is an insect pest preventing cattle and oxen (Option C) from thriving.
fields.passage_excerpt: only small numbers of cattle or oxen are kept in the province owing to the prevalence of the tsetse fly.
fields.what_question_asks: Which animals cannot be raised in large numbers because of harmful insects.
fields.what_passage_says: 'only small numbers of cattle or oxen are kept in the province owing to the prevalence of the tsetse fly'.
fields.why_answer: The tsetse fly is an insect pest preventing cattle and oxen (Option C) from thriving.
fields.paraphrase: insect pests -> tsetse fly; do not thrive -> only small numbers ... are kept
fields.tip: The tsetse fly is a well-known African insect pest that attacks cattle and oxen.

fields.question_text: They are often preserved and sold outside the local area.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 6-9) and the list of animals below. Match each statement with the correct animal, A, B or C.
fields.explanation: Drying fish preserves it for trade to distant regions, pointing to Fish (Option A).
fields.passage_excerpt: Much fish is dried for sale to areas away from the main waterways.
fields.what_question_asks: Which food product is preserved and transported for sale away from the local waterways.
fields.what_passage_says: 'Much fish is dried for sale to areas away from the main waterways'.
fields.why_answer: Drying fish preserves it for trade to distant regions, pointing to Fish (Option A).
fields.paraphrase: preserved and sold outside the local area -> dried for sale to areas away from the main waterways
fields.tip: 'Dried for sale' is the traditional preservation method.

fields.question_text: Agricultural land is usually prepared without the help of oxen.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1? Choose TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: Because animal power is absent and work is done by hand-hoeing, land is indeed prepared without oxen. The statement is TRUE.
fields.passage_excerpt: The resulting absence of animal power for pulling machinery greatly limits people's ability to plough and cultivate land: a married couple can rarely manage to prepare an area of more than half a hectare by hand-hoeing.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether farmers typically prepare their fields without using draught oxen.
fields.what_passage_says: Due to tsetse flies, there is an 'absence of animal power for pulling machinery' and land is prepared by hand-hoeing.
fields.why_answer: Because animal power is absent and work is done by hand-hoeing, land is indeed prepared without oxen. The statement is TRUE.
fields.paraphrase: without the help of oxen -> absence of animal power ... prepare ... by hand-hoeing
fields.tip: 'Absence of animal power' confirms no oxen are used.

fields.question_text: Children are a source of extra labour during busy periods.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1? Choose TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: Children's participation in agricultural work is never mentioned in the text.
fields.passage_excerpt: Richards (1969) observed that the practice of citemene entails a definite division of labour; men and women perform different tasks.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether children are brought in to assist with agricultural tasks during peak seasons.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage details the division of labor between adult men and women, but says nothing about children working.
fields.why_answer: Children's participation in agricultural work is never mentioned in the text.
fields.paraphrase: No information regarding child labor or children helping on farms.
fields.tip: If child labor is completely unmentioned in the passage, the answer is NOT GIVEN.

fields.question_text: The people of Luapula Province eat chicken on a regular basis.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1? Choose TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: 'Not a standard part of most people's diet' directly contradicts the claim that they eat chicken on a regular basis. The answer is FALSE.
fields.passage_excerpt: These animals are not a standard part of most people's diet.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether chicken is a common, regularly consumed staple in Luapula.
fields.what_passage_says: Referring to chickens and goats, the text explicitly notes: 'These animals are not a standard part of most people's diet.'
fields.why_answer: 'Not a standard part of most people's diet' directly contradicts the claim that they eat chicken on a regular basis. The answer is FALSE.
fields.paraphrase: eat chicken on a regular basis contradicts: not a standard part of most people's diet
fields.tip: 'Not a standard part of the diet' means it is rarely eaten, not eaten regularly.

fields.question_text: What is the writer's opinion about traditional farming methods in Luapula Province?
fields.question_instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
fields.explanation: Option C, 'They will be inadequate to support a growing population', directly paraphrases 'not capable ... of supporting the expanding population'.
fields.passage_excerpt: neither the fisheries nor the woodlands of Luapula are capable, with unmodified traditional practices, of supporting the expanding population in a sustainable manner.
fields.what_question_asks: What conclusion the author draws regarding the future sustainability of traditional farming methods.
fields.what_passage_says: Traditional practices are not capable of supporting the expanding population sustainably, and future diets will suffer unless systems are intensified and diversified.
fields.why_answer: Option C, 'They will be inadequate to support a growing population', directly paraphrases 'not capable ... of supporting the expanding population'.
fields.paraphrase: inadequate to support a growing population -> not capable ... of supporting the expanding population
fields.tip: Focus on the concluding warning in the final paragraph.

fields.question_text: a description of the methodology of an experiment carried out by several research institutes
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A-H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-H.
fields.explanation: The experimental procedure involving 60 babies and microphone recordings across multiple institutes is the methodology in Paragraph E.
fields.passage_excerpt: These three research groups made a comparison of recordings of 60 healthy newborns aged between two and five days old: 30 infants born into French-speaking families and 30 born into German-speaking families.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph details the testing process and recordings conducted jointly by the German and French research teams.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph E describes how the three research groups recorded 60 newborns (30 French, 30 German) with microphones for over 20 hours and fed the audio into a computer.
fields.why_answer: The experimental procedure involving 60 babies and microphone recordings across multiple institutes is the methodology in Paragraph E.
fields.paraphrase: methodology of an experiment carried out by several research institutes -> three research groups made a comparison of recordings of 60 healthy newborns
fields.tip: Look for numbers of participants, age ranges, and data recording procedures.

fields.question_text: the rationale for choosing the participants of an experiment
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A-H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-H.
fields.explanation: Explaining the reason for selecting German and French babies provides the rationale for choosing the participants (Paragraph D).
fields.passage_excerpt: German and French babies were selected for the comparison because the differences in the intonation shapes of these two mother tongues are particularly pronounced.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph explains why researchers specifically selected German and French infants.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph D explains that German and French babies were chosen 'because the differences in the intonation shapes of these two mother tongues are particularly pronounced'.
fields.why_answer: Explaining the reason for selecting German and French babies provides the rationale for choosing the participants (Paragraph D).
fields.paraphrase: rationale for choosing the participants -> German and French babies were selected ... because the differences ... are particularly pronounced
fields.tip: 'Rationale' means the underlying reason or justification for a choice.

fields.question_text: a suggestion that babies are driven to copy their mothers to gain food
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A-H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-H.
fields.explanation: 'Physical nourishment' means food, and 'motivated to imitate' means driven to copy (Paragraph F).
fields.passage_excerpt: Newborns are probably highly motivated to imitate their mother's behaviour in order to attract her and foster bonding and therefore physical nourishment," they wrote.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph hypothesizes that infants imitate maternal vocal patterns to secure feeding/nutrition.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph F states: 'Newborns are probably highly motivated to imitate their mother's behaviour in order to attract her and foster bonding and therefore physical nourishment'.
fields.why_answer: 'Physical nourishment' means food, and 'motivated to imitate' means driven to copy (Paragraph F).
fields.paraphrase: driven to copy their mothers to gain food -> motivated to imitate their mother's behaviour in order to ... foster ... physical nourishment
fields.tip: 'Physical nourishment' is a direct formal synonym for food/feeding.

fields.question_text: an account of the methodology of a past experiment carried out by the Leipzig researchers
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A-H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-H.
fields.explanation: This describes the procedure of an earlier (past) experiment by the Leipzig team (Paragraph B).
fields.passage_excerpt: The Leipzig researchers showed that in an earlier experiment, by means of physiological studies of babies of three to four months of age. For that study, the babies had hoods with electrodes put on their heads, and had recordings of different intonation patterns played to them.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph explains how an earlier study with electrode hoods was performed in Leipzig.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph B reports an earlier experiment where Leipzig researchers placed electrode hoods on 3-to-4-month-old babies and played varying intonation audio.
fields.why_answer: This describes the procedure of an earlier (past) experiment by the Leipzig team (Paragraph B).
fields.paraphrase: methodology of a past experiment -> in an earlier experiment ... had hoods with electrodes put on their heads
fields.tip: 'Earlier experiment' matches 'past experiment'.

fields.question_text: an illustration of the limitation of babies' ability to hear inside the womb
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A-H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-H.
fields.explanation: The bathtub metaphor provides an illustration of the foetus's auditory limitations (Paragraph A).
fields.passage_excerpt: Human foetuses perceive information filtered at around 400 hertz, but they cannot hear the actual words. It is a bit like holding your head under water when someone is talking next to the bath.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph gives an analogy/example illustrating how hearing is muffled in the uterus.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph A explains that fetuses cannot hear actual words, comparing it to 'holding your head under water when someone is talking next to the bath'.
fields.why_answer: The bathtub metaphor provides an illustration of the foetus's auditory limitations (Paragraph A).
fields.paraphrase: illustration of the limitation -> like holding your head under water when someone is talking next to the bath
fields.tip: An analogy using 'like...' serves as an illustration.

fields.question_text: an assertion that babies of different nationalities cry with different intonation
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A-H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A-H.
fields.explanation: Comparing German and French babies' distinct melodic contours confirms that different nationalities cry with different intonation (Paragraph F).
fields.passage_excerpt: The melody of the German babies' screams usually began loudly and at a high pitch and then followed a downward curve, while the French babies more often screamed with a rising melody contour.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph confirms that infants from different language backgrounds cry using different melody shapes.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph F states German babies scream with a downward curve while French babies cry with a rising contour, reproducing their native intonation.
fields.why_answer: Comparing German and French babies' distinct melodic contours confirms that different nationalities cry with different intonation (Paragraph F).
fields.paraphrase: different nationalities cry with different intonation -> German babies ... downward curve, while French babies ... rising melody contour
fields.tip: Notice the specific contrast between German and French infants.

fields.question_text: Important everyday sounds must remain consistent in order to be understood.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 20-23) and the list of researchers below. Match each statement with the correct researcher, A, B or C.
fields.explanation: Dr Katya Williams (Option B) compared consistent crying to an unchanging fire siren alarm.
fields.passage_excerpt: This assumption was corrected when we noticed that the cries are not the same from week to week. What biological purpose would that have? If a fire siren sounded different every day, we would not even recognise it!"
fields.what_question_asks: Which researcher used the analogy that crucial alert sounds must stay recognizable like a fire siren.
fields.what_passage_says: Dr Katya Williams observed: 'If a fire siren sounded different every day, we would not even recognise it!'
fields.why_answer: Dr Katya Williams (Option B) compared consistent crying to an unchanging fire siren alarm.
fields.paraphrase: everyday sounds must remain consistent -> if a fire siren sounded different every day, we would not even recognise it
fields.tip: The fire siren metaphor belongs to Dr Katya Williams in paragraph C.

fields.question_text: The different tones used in crying help babies to learn language later on.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 20-23) and the list of researchers below. Match each statement with the correct researcher, A, B or C.
fields.explanation: Mr Walter Meade (Option C) linked crying melody patterns to later linguistic acquisition.
fields.passage_excerpt: The melodic patterns practised in crying are building blocks for eventual sound production, such as gurgling and babbling, right up to the first words and sentences," says Meade.
fields.what_question_asks: Which researcher stated that melody practice in crying forms the stepping stones for speech.
fields.what_passage_says: Mr Walter Meade discovered that initial sensitivity assists infants in subsequent language learning and that crying melodies are 'building blocks for eventual sound production... right up to first words'.
fields.why_answer: Mr Walter Meade (Option C) linked crying melody patterns to later linguistic acquisition.
fields.paraphrase: help babies to learn language later on -> building blocks for eventual sound production ... first words and sentences
fields.tip: 'Building blocks' indicates developmental preparation.

fields.question_text: The tune of young primates' cries is created by their breathing, not their brain.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 20-23) and the list of researchers below. Match each statement with the correct researcher, A, B or C.
fields.explanation: Dr Katya Williams (Option B) noted that chimp crying is respiratory rather than mental.
fields.passage_excerpt: According to Williams, among baby chimpanzees, the 'crying melody' is closely associated with the build-up and reduction of pressure in the lungs, and is not generated by a mental process.
fields.what_question_asks: Which researcher noted that chimpanzee infant cries arise from physical respiration rather than cognition.
fields.what_passage_says: Dr Katya Williams explained that among infant chimps, crying melody is linked to lung pressure and 'not generated by a mental process'.
fields.why_answer: Dr Katya Williams (Option B) noted that chimp crying is respiratory rather than mental.
fields.paraphrase: breathing, not their brain -> pressure in the lungs, and is not generated by a mental process
fields.tip: 'Not generated by a mental process' means not by their brain.

fields.question_text: Unborn babies in the womb are focused on the voice of one specific person.
fields.question_instructions: Look at the following statements (Questions 20-23) and the list of researchers below. Match each statement with the correct researcher, A, B or C.
fields.explanation: Professor Amelia Finlayson (Option A) identified that the fetus specifically senses the mother's voice.
fields.passage_excerpt: The mother's voice in particular is sensed early on," explains Professor Amelia Finlayson
fields.what_question_asks: Which researcher found that the fetus pays special attention to the mother's voice.
fields.what_passage_says: Professor Amelia Finlayson explains: 'The mother's voice in particular is sensed early on'.
fields.why_answer: Professor Amelia Finlayson (Option A) identified that the fetus specifically senses the mother's voice.
fields.paraphrase: voice of one specific person -> mother's voice in particular
fields.tip: 'In particular' means specially focused on one.

fields.question_text: Professor Amelia Finlayson doubts unborn babies can recognise different ___
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentences below. Write ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
fields.explanation: 'Accents' is the exact word in the passage describing what babies cannot tell apart.
fields.passage_excerpt: Finlayson's research indicates that newborn babies probably cannot distinguish between the accents of Welsh and Northern Scottish people or between Low German and Upper Bavarian
fields.what_question_asks: What vocal or regional variation babies cannot distinguish between.
fields.what_passage_says: Research indicates newborns cannot distinguish between the 'accents' of regional speakers.
fields.why_answer: 'Accents' is the exact word in the passage describing what babies cannot tell apart.
fields.paraphrase: cannot distinguish between -> doubts unborn babies can recognise; different ___ -> accents
fields.tip: Identify what Welsh, Scottish, and Bavarian represent: regional accents.

fields.question_text: In the first Leipzig experiment, the ___ of babies changed upon hearing different intonation patterns.
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentences below. Write ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
fields.explanation: 'Brainwaves' is the physical response detected by the electrode hoods.
fields.passage_excerpt: The children's brainwaves reacted to the differences even when they were asleep.
fields.what_question_asks: What neurological signals in the babies reacted when played different intonation recordings.
fields.what_passage_says: 'The children's brainwaves reacted to the differences even when they were asleep.'
fields.why_answer: 'Brainwaves' is the physical response detected by the electrode hoods.
fields.paraphrase: changed upon hearing -> reacted to the differences
fields.tip: The electrode hoods measured brainwaves.

fields.question_text: Early scientists believed that babies cried for no other reason than as a ___ that they wanted their parents.
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentences below. Write ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
fields.explanation: 'Signal' is the exact noun filling the blank in the sentence.
fields.passage_excerpt: It used to be thought that a baby's cry was just a signal of alarm to call its mother.
fields.what_question_asks: What past researchers considered crying to be, prior to realizing it was linguistic.
fields.what_passage_says: It was previously believed crying was 'just a signal of alarm to call its mother'.
fields.why_answer: 'Signal' is the exact noun filling the blank in the sentence.
fields.paraphrase: cried for no other reason than as a ___ -> just a signal of alarm to call its mother
fields.tip: 'Just a signal' matches 'for no other reason than as a signal'.

fields.question_text: Historians have expressed little curiosity about the rise of the Roman Empire.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 3? Choose YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: Constantly asking the question across centuries shows intense curiosity, directly contradicting 'little curiosity'. The answer is NO.
fields.passage_excerpt: From ancient times to the present, historians have asked the question: How and why did an ordinary little town in central Italy grow so much bigger than any other in the ancient Mediterranean and come to control such a huge empire?
fields.what_question_asks: Whether historians have shown little interest in the growth and expansion of Rome.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage says that 'from ancient times to the present, historians have asked the question' of how and why Rome grew to control a huge empire.
fields.why_answer: Constantly asking the question across centuries shows intense curiosity, directly contradicting 'little curiosity'. The answer is NO.
fields.paraphrase: question: 'little curiosity' contradicts passage: 'from ancient times to the present, historians have asked the question'
fields.tip: Asking questions across eras indicates great curiosity, not little curiosity.

fields.question_text: Accounts from the first century BCE of Rome's origins may be less reliable than 21st-century accounts.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 3? Choose YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: Having less direct evidence makes their accounts potentially less reliable than modern ones, agreeing with the statement (YES).
fields.passage_excerpt: Yet these historians had little more direct evidence of the earliest phases of Rome's history than modern writers have, and in some ways perhaps not as much, as there were no surviving documents or archives.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether first-century BCE historical accounts had less direct evidence and reliability than modern ones.
fields.what_passage_says: The author notes that ancient writers had 'little more direct evidence... and in some ways perhaps not as much' because they lacked surviving archives.
fields.why_answer: Having less direct evidence makes their accounts potentially less reliable than modern ones, agreeing with the statement (YES).
fields.paraphrase: less reliable -> had little more direct evidence ... and in some ways perhaps not as much
fields.tip: Having less factual evidence directly relates to lower reliability.

fields.question_text: Most Roman historians viewed their ancient capital in an unrealistically positive light.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 3? Choose YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: The text mentions they wrote about their 'failings' as well as values, and never states they held an unrealistically positive view.
fields.passage_excerpt: Their 'histories' about the foundation of ancient Rome tell us a good deal about how the Romans saw their city, their values, and their failings.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether early Roman historians had a biased, excessively flattering view of Rome.
fields.what_passage_says: The author says Roman histories tell us how they saw their city, including 'their values, and their failings', without asserting that most viewed it unrealistically positively.
fields.why_answer: The text mentions they wrote about their 'failings' as well as values, and never states they held an unrealistically positive view.
fields.paraphrase: No statement that historians held an 'unrealistically positive' perspective.
fields.tip: Mention of 'failings' actually shows they acknowledged shortcomings, but the specific claim is NOT GIVEN.

fields.question_text: The accounts by early Roman historians about the founding of Rome provide a full description of life at that time.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 3? Choose YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: Telling 'very little indeed' directly contradicts 'provide a full description'. The answer is NO.
fields.passage_excerpt: However, they tell us very little indeed about what they claim to inform us about: that is, what earliest Rome was actually like.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether early Roman writings offer a comprehensive picture of early Roman life.
fields.what_passage_says: 'However, they tell us very little indeed about what they claim to inform us about: that is, what earliest Rome was actually like.'
fields.why_answer: Telling 'very little indeed' directly contradicts 'provide a full description'. The answer is NO.
fields.paraphrase: full description contradicts: tell us very little indeed about what earliest Rome was actually like
fields.tip: 'Very little indeed' is the opposite of 'a full description'.

fields.question_text: It is certain that the city of Rome was in existence long before 63 BCE.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 3? Choose YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: 'One fact is obvious' and 'already a very old city' confirms the statement as YES.
fields.passage_excerpt: One fact is obvious. Rome was already a very old city by 63 BCE, the birth date of its first emperor.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether it is undisputed that Rome existed well before 63 BCE.
fields.what_passage_says: 'One fact is obvious. Rome was already a very old city by 63 BCE, the birth date of its first emperor.'
fields.why_answer: 'One fact is obvious' and 'already a very old city' confirms the statement as YES.
fields.paraphrase: It is certain -> One fact is obvious; in existence long before -> already a very old city
fields.tip: 'One fact is obvious' means it is certain.

fields.question_text: Some people oppose archaeological excavations in Rome because they can damage the ancient monuments.
