fields.tip: The original answer review lists two acceptable forms; either is keyed as correct.

fields.question_text: Taste is supposed to help us differentiate food that’s ___ for us from food that’s not.
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentence. Choose ONE word from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 6–11 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: The passage directly describes food that is good for us.
fields.passage_excerpt: Taste is supposed to help us differentiate food that’s good for us from food that’s not.
fields.what_question_asks: Which word describes the food taste helps us distinguish as beneficial.
fields.what_passage_says: Taste helps differentiate food that is good for us from food that is not.
fields.why_answer: The missing word is stated exactly in the passage: ‘good’.
fields.paraphrase: The sentence completion repeats the passage’s ‘good for us’ phrase.
fields.tip: Use the exact word from the passage.

fields.question_text: Indeed this ___ for flavour was, in the past, the reason why so many explorers ventured to distant lands to bring back new.
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentence. Choose ONE word from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 6–11 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: The review key gives ‘aroma’ for this blank.
fields.passage_excerpt: The human craving for flavour has been a large unacknowledged and unexamined force in history.
fields.what_question_asks: Which word completes the phrase describing a driver behind exploration.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage connects the human craving for flavour with explorers travelling to distant lands to obtain seasonings.
fields.why_answer: The source review explicitly keys ‘aroma’ for this blank; it is the requested word in the sentence-completion exercise.
fields.paraphrase: The prompt links a flavour-related motive with the passage’s discussion of exploration and seasonings.
fields.tip: Follow the answer shown in the source review rather than substituting a related word.

fields.question_text: Explorers ventured to distant lands to bring back new ___ which were greatly sought after in Europe.
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentence. Choose ONE word from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 6–11 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: The passage explicitly says Columbus sought new seasonings.
fields.passage_excerpt: In 1492, Christopher Columbus set sail in order to try to find new seasonings and thus to make his fortune with this most desired commodity of that time.
fields.what_question_asks: What explorers sought and brought back from distant lands.
fields.what_passage_says: Columbus set out to find new seasonings, described as a highly desired commodity.
fields.why_answer: ‘Seasonings’ is the word used in the passage and is the answer recorded by the source review.
fields.paraphrase: ‘bring back new’ corresponds to Columbus trying to ‘find new seasonings’.
fields.tip: Copy the exact plural form from the text.

fields.question_text: They were used in cooking to enhance the usual ___ and unappetizing dishes eaten by rich and poor alike.
fields.question_instructions: Complete the sentence. Choose ONE word from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 6–11 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: The review key gives ‘flavour’ for this sentence-completion item.
fields.passage_excerpt: The rise and fall of corporate empires – soft-drink companies, snack-food companies, and fast-food chains – is frequently determined by how their products taste.
fields.what_question_asks: Which word completes the phrase about improving dishes.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage repeatedly discusses flavour as the desired quality in foods and says product success is determined by taste.
fields.why_answer: The source review records ‘flavour’ as the answer to the blank.
fields.paraphrase: The prompt asks for the quality in food that cooking ingredients enhance.
fields.tip: Preserve the British spelling used in the source.

fields.question_text: We associate certain smells with the past as they are ___.
fields.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from Reading Passage 1 for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 12–13 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: The flavours of childhood foods leave an indelible mark, providing the keyed word.
fields.passage_excerpt: The flavours of childhood foods seem to leave an indelible mark, and adults often return to them, without always knowing why.
fields.what_question_asks: Why certain smells are associated with the past.
fields.what_passage_says: Childhood flavours leave an indelible mark, while aromas and memories are closely linked.
fields.why_answer: The passage’s exact word describing the lasting mark is ‘indelible’, which is the answer given in the source review.
fields.paraphrase: ‘associate certain smells with the past’ links to the passage’s memory connection and ‘indelible mark’.
fields.tip: The answer must be taken from the passage and fit the two-word maximum.

fields.question_text: Modern technology is able to help determine the minute quantities of ___ found in food.
fields.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from Reading Passage 1 for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 12–13 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: Modern instruments detect chemical aromas in very small quantities.
fields.passage_excerpt: Today’s sophisticated spectrometers, gas chromatograph, and headspace vapor analyzers provide a detailed map of a food’s flavour components, detecting chemical aromas in amounts as low as one part per billion.
fields.what_question_asks: What modern technology can measure in minute quantities in food.
fields.what_passage_says: The instruments detect chemical aromas in amounts as low as one part per billion.
fields.why_answer: The exact two-word phrase in the passage is ‘chemical aromas’, matching the answer shown in the source review.
fields.paraphrase: ‘minute quantities’ paraphrases ‘amounts as low as one part per billion’.
fields.tip: Keep the exact two-word phrase from the passage.

fields.question_text: A reference to the irregular movement of particles.
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H. Which paragraph contains the following information? You may use any letter more than once.
fields.explanation: Paragraph B describes particles vibrating, being lifted, and then jerking other particles into the air.
fields.passage_excerpt: When a steady wind starts to blow, fine particles on the open ground will begin vibrating.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph describes particles moving irregularly.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph B says particles vibrate, rise, fall, and set off a chain reaction.
fields.why_answer: The vibrating and jerking movements are a direct match for irregular movement.
fields.paraphrase: ‘irregular movement’ paraphrases particles ‘begin vibrating’ and are ‘jerked into the air’.
fields.tip: Scan for descriptions of particle motion, especially verbs such as vibrate and jerk.

fields.question_text: Mention of a productive land turning into a desert in the 20th century.
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H. Which paragraph contains the following information? You may use any letter more than once.
fields.explanation: Paragraph G describes American farmland that became desert during the 20th century.
fields.passage_excerpt: In the 20th century, one of the states of America had a large section of farmland that had turned into desert.
fields.what_question_asks: Where the passage refers to productive farmland becoming desert in the 20th century.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph G identifies a large area of American farmland that had turned into desert.
fields.why_answer: This paragraph contains both the farmland-to-desert change and the specified century.
fields.paraphrase: ‘productive land’ refers to the farmland that ‘had turned into desert’.
fields.tip: Match the time reference and the land-use change together.

fields.question_text: Types of deserts.
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H. Which paragraph contains the following information? You may use any letter more than once.
fields.explanation: Paragraph A explains how deserts are classified using precipitation, rainfall days, temperature, humidity, and other factors.
fields.passage_excerpt: Deserts have been classified in a number of ways, generally combining total precipitation, how many days the rainfall occurs, temperature, humidity, and sometimes additional factors.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph describes categories or types of deserts.
fields.what_passage_says: Paragraph A lists the factors used in classifying deserts.
fields.why_answer: The classification statement is the passage’s reference to different types of deserts.
fields.paraphrase: ‘types of deserts’ corresponds to how deserts ‘have been classified’.
fields.tip: Look for explicit language about classification.

fields.question_text: Mention of technical methods used to tackle the problems of deserts.
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H. Which paragraph contains the following information? You may use any letter more than once.
fields.explanation: Paragraph H mentions satellites being used to investigate the effects of people and livestock.
fields.passage_excerpt: Satellites have been utilized to investigate the influence that people and livestock have on our planet Earth.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph mentions technical methods addressing desertification.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage names satellites as a technology used to investigate human and livestock influence.
fields.why_answer: Satellites are the technical method referred to in the question, and they appear in Paragraph H.
fields.paraphrase: ‘technical methods’ refers to the use of satellites.
fields.tip: Locate the paragraph naming the technology rather than broader social responses.

fields.question_text: The influence of a traditional way of feeding animals on desertification.
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H. Which paragraph contains the following information? You may use any letter more than once.
fields.explanation: Paragraph D explains that overgrazing removes vegetation and exposes soil to erosion.
fields.passage_excerpt: When a specific field is used to graze an excessive herd, it will experience a loss in vegetation coverage, and the soil will be trampled as well as be pulverized.
fields.what_question_asks: How a traditional animal-feeding or grazing practice affects desertification.
fields.what_passage_says: Excessive grazing reduces vegetation and damages soil, leaving it exposed to erosion.
fields.why_answer: The described effects of grazing are directly linked in the paragraph to advancing desertification.
fields.paraphrase: ‘feeding animals’ refers to grazing herds; ‘influence’ refers to vegetation loss and erosion.
fields.tip: Follow the cause-and-effect chain from grazing to soil erosion.

fields.question_text: A lack of agreement among scientists about the causes of desertification.
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H. Which paragraph contains the following information? You may use any letter more than once.
fields.explanation: Paragraph C says the academic community has never agreed on the causes of desertification.
fields.passage_excerpt: There has been a tremendous deal of publicity on how severe desertification can be, but the academic circle has never agreed on the causes of desertification.
fields.what_question_asks: Where the passage says scientists do not agree about the causes.
fields.what_passage_says: The academic circle has never agreed on the causes of desertification.
fields.why_answer: This is an explicit statement of disagreement among academics.
fields.paraphrase: ‘lack of agreement among scientists’ paraphrases ‘the academic circle has never agreed’.
fields.tip: Look for wording that signals disagreement or uncertainty.

fields.question_text: A description of the adverse effects of growing food crops.
fields.question_instructions: Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H. Which paragraph contains the following information? You may use any letter more than once.
fields.explanation: Paragraph C explains that crop cultivation removes vegetation and leaves land vulnerable to erosion after crop failures.
fields.passage_excerpt: The raising of most crops requires the natural vegetation cover to be removed first; when crop failures occur, extensive tracts of land are devoid of a plant cover and thus susceptible to wind and water erosion.
fields.what_question_asks: Which paragraph describes negative effects associated with growing crops.
fields.what_passage_says: Removing vegetation for crops and subsequent crop failures can leave large areas exposed to erosion.
fields.why_answer: The paragraph explicitly links crop cultivation and crop failure with loss of plant cover and erosion.
fields.paraphrase: ‘adverse effects’ refers to vegetation removal and increased erosion risk.
fields.tip: Find the paragraph connecting crop growing with environmental consequences.

fields.question_text: It is difficult to ascertain where the deserts end in some areas.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 2? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: The passage says some deserts have no clear-cut borders with other landscape features.
fields.passage_excerpt: In some places, deserts have clear boundaries marked by rivers, mountains or other landforms, while in other places, there are no clear-cut borders between desert and other landscape features.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether some desert boundaries are hard to identify.
fields.what_passage_says: Some places have no clear-cut border between desert and other landscape features.
fields.why_answer: An unclear border makes it difficult to determine where the desert ends, so the statement agrees.
fields.paraphrase: ‘difficult to ascertain where the deserts end’ paraphrases ‘no clear-cut borders’.
fields.tip: Compare the statement with the passage’s contrast between clear and unclear boundaries.

fields.question_text: The media is uninterested in the problems of desertification.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 2? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: The passage says there has been a tremendous deal of publicity about desertification, contradicting the claim of media disinterest.
fields.passage_excerpt: There has been a tremendous deal of publicity on how severe desertification can be.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether media attention to desertification is lacking.
fields.what_passage_says: There has been considerable publicity about the severity of desertification.
fields.why_answer: Considerable publicity is the opposite of being uninterested, so the statement is FALSE.
fields.paraphrase: ‘uninterested’ contradicts ‘a tremendous deal of publicity’.
fields.tip: Watch for direct opposites in statements about the amount of publicity.

fields.question_text: The most common cause of desertification is the lack of rainfall.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 2? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: The passage calls rainfall shortage a common misunderstanding and says human activities are more often responsible.
fields.passage_excerpt: A common misunderstanding is that a shortage of precipitation causes the desertification… In fact, more often than not, human activities are responsible for desertification.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether a lack of rainfall is the most common cause of desertification.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage rejects this as a common misunderstanding and identifies human activities as the more frequent cause.
fields.why_answer: The passage directly contradicts the claim that rainfall shortage is the most common cause.
fields.paraphrase: ‘lack of rainfall’ is contradicted by ‘human activities are responsible’.
fields.tip: Do not mistake an explicitly labelled misunderstanding for the author’s position.

fields.question_text: Farming animals in semi-arid areas will increase soil erosion.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 2? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: Livestock farming accelerates soil erosion, according to the passage.
fields.passage_excerpt: Livestock farming in semi-arid areas accelerates the erosion of soil and becomes one of the reasons for advancing desertification.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether raising animals in semi-arid regions increases soil erosion.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage states that livestock farming in semi-arid areas accelerates soil erosion.
fields.why_answer: The statement repeats the passage’s claim in equivalent wording, so it is TRUE.
fields.paraphrase: ‘farming animals’ means livestock farming; ‘increase’ paraphrases ‘accelerates’.
fields.tip: Match the key location and action in the statement to the passage.

fields.question_text: People in Asian countries no longer use firewood as the chief fuel.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 2? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: The passage says firewood is the chief fuel in many Asian countries, but does not state that it is no longer used.
fields.passage_excerpt: In many Asian countries, firewood is the chief fuel used for cooking and heating.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether people have stopped using firewood as their main fuel.
fields.what_passage_says: The text describes firewood as the chief fuel in many Asian countries.
fields.why_answer: The text gives a current use but does not discuss whether this use has ended; it does not support the claim about no longer using it.
fields.paraphrase: The statement’s ‘no longer’ is not addressed by the passage.
fields.tip: A present-tense fact alone does not establish a change over time.

fields.question_text: Technology studying the relationship of people, livestock and desertification has not yet been invented.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 2? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: Satellites are already used to investigate the influence of people and livestock.
fields.passage_excerpt: Satellites have been utilized to investigate the influence that people and livestock have on our planet Earth.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether no technology exists to study people, livestock, and their impact.
fields.what_passage_says: Satellites have already been utilized to investigate the influence of people and livestock.
fields.why_answer: The passage gives an existing technology for this investigation, contradicting the claim that none has been invented.
fields.paraphrase: ‘has not yet been invented’ is contradicted by ‘have been utilized’.
fields.tip: Look for evidence that the method already exists.

fields.question_text: As expected, the artworks chosen for the exhibition reflect a narrow interpretation of landscape.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: The writer says the exhibition creates a flexible, wide-ranging notion of landscape, the opposite of a narrow interpretation.
fields.passage_excerpt: It is hardly surprising, then, that this results in a flexible, wide-ranging notion of landscape.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether the writer considers the exhibition’s landscape interpretation narrow.
fields.what_passage_says: The writer describes it as flexible and wide-ranging.
fields.why_answer: A flexible, wide-ranging notion contradicts the statement’s narrow interpretation, so the answer is NO.
fields.paraphrase: ‘narrow interpretation’ contrasts with ‘flexible, wide-ranging notion’.
fields.tip: For YES/NO questions, compare the writer’s expressed view with the statement.

fields.question_text: The Academy rejected Australian suggestions for the subject of the exhibition.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: The passage discusses the chosen subject and concerns about British influence, but does not say the Academy rejected Australian suggestions.
fields.passage_excerpt: there is a suggestion that British artistic values have directed this exhibition, rather than allowing Australia the freedom to demonstrate its maturity.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether the Academy rejected suggestions from Australians about the exhibition’s subject.
fields.what_passage_says: The passage raises concerns about British influence but does not mention any Australian suggestions being rejected.
fields.why_answer: No statement confirms or denies that suggestions were made and rejected, so this view is not given.
fields.paraphrase: The passage’s discussion of influence does not establish that suggestions were rejected.
fields.tip: Do not infer a specific rejection from a general criticism of influence.

fields.question_text: The colonial relationship meant that early Australian landscape painting followed the traditions of English landscape painting.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: The writer says colonial ties led early Australian art to reflect Britain’s devotion to landscape.
fields.passage_excerpt: Because of colonial ties, it was inevitable during Australian art's formative years that it would reflect Britain's devotion to the beloved landscape before its own character and idiosyncrasies took shape.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether colonial ties caused early Australian landscape art to follow a British tradition.
fields.what_passage_says: Early Australian art reflected Britain’s devotion to landscape before developing its own character.
fields.why_answer: This directly supports the statement’s link between the colonial relationship and British landscape tradition.
fields.paraphrase: ‘followed the traditions of English landscape painting’ paraphrases ‘reflect Britain's devotion to the beloved landscape’.
fields.tip: Match the historical cause and influence, not just the shared subject.

fields.question_text: The exhibition reflects the fact that Australian art developed its own particular qualities.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: The writer says the Academy embraces the peculiarities of Australian art and Soriano wanted to show its distinctiveness.
fields.passage_excerpt: the Academy is nevertheless embracing the peculiarities of Australian art from the mid-19th century onward
fields.what_question_asks: Whether the exhibition shows Australian art’s distinctive qualities.
fields.what_passage_says: The Academy embraces Australian art’s peculiarities, and Soriano says she wanted to show its distinctiveness.
fields.why_answer: Both statements affirm that Australian art’s particular characteristics are present in the exhibition.
fields.paraphrase: ‘particular qualities’ paraphrases ‘peculiarities’ and ‘distinctiveness’.
fields.tip: Look for words indicating uniqueness or distinctiveness.

fields.question_text: Contemporary Australian artists have generally rejected British landscape traditions.
fields.question_instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer? Write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.
fields.explanation: The passage says British landscape remains relevant, but does not say Australian artists have generally rejected it.
fields.passage_excerpt: there can be little denying that British landscape painting is still relevant to a current generation of Australian practitioners, however indirectly.
fields.what_question_asks: Whether contemporary Australian artists generally rejected British landscape traditions.
fields.what_passage_says: British landscape painting remains relevant to current Australian artists, but the passage does not characterize their overall position as rejection or acceptance.
fields.why_answer: The relevance of a tradition does not establish the claim that artists generally rejected it; that generalization is not given.
fields.paraphrase: The text says ‘still relevant’, not that artists have ‘generally rejected’ the tradition.
fields.tip: Avoid turning a statement about relevance into a claim about what most artists reject.

fields.question_text: What is the writer's main point in the second paragraph?
fields.question_instructions: Choose the correct letter. Write the correct letter, A, B, C or D, in boxes 32–36 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: The paragraph questions whether British artistic values have directed the exhibition instead of allowing Australian art to show its maturity.
fields.passage_excerpt: there is a suggestion that British artistic values have directed this exhibition, rather than allowing Australia the freedom to demonstrate its maturity.
fields.what_question_asks: The main argument made in the passage’s second numbered paragraph.
fields.what_passage_says: The writer describes concern that British values directed the exhibition rather than allowing Australian art to demonstrate its maturity.
fields.why_answer: This concern is captured by option C, that Britain is still imposing principles on Australian art. The other options make claims not stated in this paragraph.
fields.paraphrase: ‘British artistic values have directed’ the exhibition maps to British influence over Australian art.
fields.tip: Choose the option that summarizes the paragraph’s argument rather than one supporting detail.

fields.question_text: What does Joanna Mendelssohn find surprising?
fields.question_instructions: Choose the correct letter. Write the correct letter, A, B, C or D, in boxes 32–36 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: Mendelssohn found the underlying rules for selecting works surprisingly conservative.
fields.passage_excerpt: What Mendelssohn found surprising about the exhibition was the underlying rules for the selection of works seemed to have been so conservative.
fields.what_question_asks: What aspect of the exhibition Mendelssohn found surprising.
fields.what_passage_says: She was surprised by the conservative underlying selection rules.
fields.why_answer: Option B restates the conservative, traditional nature of those selection guidelines.
fields.paraphrase: ‘very traditional’ paraphrases ‘so conservative’.
fields.tip: Locate the passage’s direct description of what she found surprising.

fields.question_text: Shaun Gladwell's work is included in the exhibition because
fields.question_instructions: Choose the correct letter. Write the correct letter, A, B, C or D, in boxes 32–36 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: Gladwell acknowledges landscape tradition but makes it personal through his own experience and individualism.
fields.passage_excerpt: It is his acknowledgement of landscape (or seascape) tradition, coloured by Gladwell's own individualism.
fields.what_question_asks: Why Gladwell’s work is included in the exhibition.
fields.what_passage_says: His work acknowledges landscape tradition while being coloured by his individualism and personal experience.
fields.why_answer: Option A captures this personal, subjective treatment. The passage does not claim that the other listed details are the reason for inclusion.
fields.paraphrase: ‘subjective approach’ maps to the tradition being ‘coloured by Gladwell's own individualism’.
fields.tip: Look for the author’s explanation of how his work relates to landscape tradition.

fields.question_text: What was the reason for Soriano including Aboriginal art in the exhibition?
fields.question_instructions: Choose the correct letter. Write the correct letter, A, B, C or D, in boxes 32–36 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: Soriano wanted Indigenous art to be seen as part of Australian art history rather than as a separate exhibition.
fields.passage_excerpt: I felt it was most accurate to be seen as part of Australian art history, rather than a separate exhibition of its own.
fields.what_question_asks: Why Soriano included Aboriginal art in this exhibition.
fields.what_passage_says: She wanted Indigenous art shown as part of Australian art history, not in a separate exhibition.
fields.why_answer: Option C matches her stated wish to integrate it into Australian art history.
fields.paraphrase: ‘part of ... tradition and not independent’ paraphrases ‘part of Australian art history, rather than a separate exhibition’.
fields.tip: Focus on Soriano’s stated reason, not the earlier exhibitions mentioned as context.

fields.question_text: By referring to China, Mendelssohn is making the point that
fields.question_instructions: Choose the correct letter. Write the correct letter, A, B, C or D, in boxes 32–36 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: Mendelssohn says London is less central to artists now, as they are interested in destinations around the world.
fields.passage_excerpt: London is increasingly less important to today's generation of artists, and this somewhat weakens the ceremony surrounding the exhibition in London.
fields.what_question_asks: What point Mendelssohn makes by citing China as an important art market.
fields.what_passage_says: London is less important to today’s generation, whose interests extend to places such as Shanghai, Venice, and Basel.
fields.why_answer: Option A summarizes the decline in London’s former status; the other options overstate or contradict the passage.
fields.paraphrase: ‘not as important as it used to be’ paraphrases ‘increasingly less important’.
fields.tip: Use the China reference in the context of the broader point about London’s changing status.

fields.question_text: In spite of its conservatism, the Royal Academy exhibition…
fields.question_instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–F. Write the correct letter, A–F, in boxes 37–40 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: Despite the conventional selection, the Academy embraces the peculiarities of Australian art.
fields.passage_excerpt: And while Mendelssohn's concern over the exhibition's conventional selection is valid, the Academy is nevertheless embracing the peculiarities of Australian art from the mid-19th century onward, albeit within the boundaries of landscape.
fields.what_question_asks: What the exhibition does despite its conservative selection.
fields.what_passage_says: The Academy embraces Australian art’s peculiarities despite the conventional selection.
fields.why_answer: Option F restates the passage’s acceptance of the distinctive features of Australian art.
fields.paraphrase: ‘in spite of its conservatism’ matches ‘while ... conventional selection’; ‘unique qualities’ matches ‘peculiarities’.
fields.tip: Use the contrast signalled by ‘while’ to match the sentence ending.

fields.question_text: Australian art of the early to mid-1800s…
fields.question_instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–F. Write the correct letter, A–F, in boxes 37–40 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: Soriano says English, French, and German art had a stronger influence in the early periods.
fields.passage_excerpt: Certainly the influence of English, French or German art is much more evident in the early periods, in the early 1800s to mid-180s.
fields.what_question_asks: What characterized Australian art of the early to mid-1800s.
fields.what_passage_says: European artistic influences were more evident in the early periods.
fields.why_answer: The European influences directly support option E, a strong European flavour.
fields.paraphrase: ‘European flavour’ paraphrases the stated influence of English, French, and German art.
fields.tip: Match the time period in the stem to Soriano’s description of early influences.

fields.question_text: The modern work by Gladwell chosen for the exhibition…
fields.question_instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–F. Write the correct letter, A–F, in boxes 37–40 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: Gladwell’s work involves the atmosphere and a storm affecting vision, connecting it to the mood of the natural environment.
fields.passage_excerpt: I was interested in Turner and the idea of atmosphere affecting vision, something I was really interested in around the time of Storm Sequence.
fields.what_question_asks: What the modern work by Gladwell reflects.
fields.what_passage_says: Gladwell links the work to atmosphere affecting vision and depicts a storm lingering offshore.
fields.why_answer: These details support option A, that the work reflects the mood created by the natural environment.
fields.paraphrase: The natural atmosphere and storm connect to the work’s environmental mood.
fields.tip: Connect the description of the work and the artist’s stated interest in atmosphere.

fields.question_text: Including Aboriginal art in the exhibition…
fields.question_instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–F. Write the correct letter, A–F, in boxes 37–40 on your answer sheet.
fields.explanation: Soriano says Australian art began in and on the landscape and uses the exhibition to bring Indigenous and settler art together.
fields.passage_excerpt: One of the reasons landscape was seen as being the right theme was because Australian art started in and on the landscape.
fields.what_question_asks: What including Aboriginal art demonstrates.
fields.what_passage_says: The exhibition places Indigenous art in relation to settlers and white Australia and relates Australian art to the land.
fields.why_answer: This supports option C’s connection to the historical importance of the land.
fields.paraphrase: ‘historical importance of the land’ corresponds to Australian art having ‘started in and on the landscape’.
fields.tip: Use the stated reason Soriano gives for bringing the different kinds of art together.

fields.question_text: Question 1: Based on Reading Passage 1, decide whether the statement follows the passage.
fields.question_instructions: Choose the correct option.

fields.question_text: The diagram shows the process of manufacturing bottled and canned water.
fields.question_instructions:
You should spend about 20 minutes on this task.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

Write at least 150 words.
fields.explanation:
Model Answer
The flow chart shows how canned and bottled water is made. In general, there are about 15
distinct stages in this linear process which can further be grouped into 5 main sets: cleaning,
carbonation, mixing, filling, and packaging.
In the first phase of the process, raw water from a tap is sent to a pump and is filtered, softened,
and chemically treated along the way. The pump then channels the water to electric heaters, from
where it is directed to a large tank of carbonation via a cooling pipe.
Once carbonated, the water is directed to a mixing tank with the use of a long pipe. In this tank,
two phases happen simultaneously, which are adding additives like coloring, syrup, and flavor to
the water and mixing the liquid with a propeller rotating in a counterclockwise direction.
Following this, the liquid is filtered again before being either bottled or canned. Finally, the
drinks are boxed and readied to be dispatched to supermarkets for consumption.
Sample 2
The chart illustrates the 5 various stages of generating containers and canned carbonated
beverages.
Overall, it is evident that there are different sections and machines in producing bottles and
beverages, beginning with the water cleaning stage and ending with packaging products.
In the first stage, raw water in the factory enters a filter for cleaning, then special equipment
creates a water softener and removes any chemical materials. In the next stage, water is pumped
to evaporate in the electric heater and then cross through a cooling pipe to make carbon dioxide,
the carbonated water remains and is sent to the next stage.

fields.question_instructions:

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

Write at least 150 words.
fields.explanation:
The diagram illustrates the process of recycling aluminium cans.
Overall, the recycling process for aluminium cans is a linear and systematic procedure that
involves collection, sorting, cleaning, melting, reshaping, and eventually reusing the
aluminium in the form of new cans. This environmentally friendly process allows a
significant portion of aluminium cans in the UK—approximately 74%—to be recycled and
reused.
To begin with, used aluminium cans must be taken to designated collection centres, rather
than being disposed of with regular household waste. From these centres, the cans are
transported to a recycling facility where they are sorted and thoroughly cleaned.
Following the cleaning stage, the cans are shredded and crushed using specialized
machinery. The shredded aluminium is then heated to a high temperature until it melts.
Once in liquid form, the aluminium is rolled out into flat sheets with a thickness ranging
between 2.5 mm and 6 mm, depending on its intended use.
The recycled aluminium is then used to produce new packaging, such as drink cans. Finally,
these newly formed cans are sent to soft drink factories, where they are filled and prepared
for sale to consumers. This cycle ensures the reuse of aluminium, reducing waste and
conserving resources
OR The diagram below show the stages in the recycling of aluminium drinks cans.

The flowchart illustrates how discarded drinks cans are recycled. Overall, this cyclical process is
composed of about eight distinct stages, which can be grouped further into three main steps:
collection, manufacturing and consumption.
At the first phase in the process, wasted cans discarded into a recycling bin are taken out and
sorted according to the material they are made of, which is either aluminum or steel. The sorted
cans are then placed into separate boxes and are transported via trucks to a recycling factory for
further processing.
In the factory, the initial stage involves compressing the delivered cans into blocks. These
blocks, in the following step, are melted down to form aluminum ingots. Next, using these
ingots, aluminum rolls are made, which serve as a raw material for new cans of standard sizes.
Ultimately, the newly recycled cans can be filled with drinks of various types, before being taken
to stock coin-operated vending machines. Once consumers purchase drinks from these machines,
empty the cans and throw them away, the cycle continues.

fields.question_text: The diagram below shows the process for recycling plastic bottles.
fields.question_instructions:
You should spend about 20 minutes on this task.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

Write at least 150 words.
fields.explanation:
The diagram provides a visual representation of the plastic bottle recycling process.
The recycling process involves nine steps, from depositing plastic bottles in specific bins to
transforming them into various end-consumer products.
Initially, individuals place plastic bottles into designated recycling bins. Subsequently,
these bottles are collected and transported to recycling centers where materials are sorted to
isolate the recyclable plastic bottles. The selected bottles are then compressed into large blocks
before being crushed into smaller pieces, which are washed and transformed into plastic pellets.
These pellets are subjected to heat to form raw materials for manufacturing a range of plastic-based
consumer goods. Finally, the raw materials are refined and processed to create products like t-
shirts, pens, plastic bottles, and containers.
After use, the end products are placed back in designated bins to continue the recycling cycle. This
comprehensive process ensures that plastic items are consistently recycled, contributing to a
sustainable and environmentally friendly approach to waste management.
Sample 2
The provided diagram vividly outlines the sequential phases involved in brick manufacturing for the
construction industry.
This process can be delineated into seven essential steps, encompassing soil excavation, sorting,
mixing, molding, drying, cooling, packaging, and delivery.
To commence, the initial step necessitates excavation of the soil surface to procure the requisite
material, typically clay. Upon arrival at the factory, the clay must undergo segregation from other
soil components. This segregation process entails the utilization of specialized machinery, including
metal grids and rollers. Subsequently, the extracted clay is amalgamated with water and sand to
create a uniform mixture, subsequently shaped into brick forms utilizing a wire cutter.
Following the molding stage, the bricks are subjected to a drying period in an oven, lasting between
24 to 48 hours. Thereafter, they are transferred to a moderate kiln, with temperatures ranging from
a minimum of 2000C to a peak of 9800C. Additionally, a high-temperature kiln, ranging from 8700C
to 13000C, is employed to further solidify the bricks before they undergo cooling and tempering in a
designated chamber.
Once fully solidified, the bricks are meticulously packaged atop wooden pallets. Upon completion of
the packaging process, they are prepared for delivery, catering to the demands of the construction
industry.

fields.question_text: The table shows data about underground railway systems in six major cities with date opened, kilometers of route and passenger numbers per year in millions.
fields.question_instructions:
You should spend about 20 minutes on this task.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

Write at least 150 words.
fields.explanation:
The table displays the date opened, the number of kilometers, and passengers each year in millions
for subway systems in various cities.
Looking from an overall perspective, it is readily apparent that the earlier underground railways
tend to be longer and now serve more passengers per year relative to the more recent ones. Tokyo
stands out for serving by far the most passengers and London for being both the oldest and largest.
London opened first (1863) and is nearly twice as expansive (394 kilometers) as the second largest
subway, in Paris, which opened in 1900 and is 199 kilometers long. However, Paris now has more
passengers compared to London (1,191,000,000 to 775,000,000). Tokyo was the next oldest having
been constructed in 1927 with routes measuring a total of 155 kilometers and being made use of by
1,928,000,000 passengers annually.
The more modern subways are Washington D.C. (1976), Kyoto (1981), and Los Angeles (2001).
Washington is the largest of the 3 at 126 kilometers with 144,000,000 yearly passengers. Kyoto is
by far the smallest (11 kilometers) and serves relatively few individuals (45 million). Similarly, the
Los Angeles subway is 18 kilometers in cumulative length and only 50,000,000 people travel on it
each year.

fields.explanation:
The table compares secondary and high school teachers' salaries in five countries in 2009.
Overall, while teachers in Luxembourg were the most well-paid, teachers from Australia were the
lowest-paid. In addition, the amount of time it took for a teacher in Denmark to earn the maximum
salary was much faster than most other countries.
Secondary and high school teachers in Luxembourg were paid a starting salary of $80,000 a year,
while the figure for teachers in Denmark was significantly lower, at $45,000. Additionally, the
starting salary for an inexperienced teacher in other countries stood at around $30,000.
However, teachers with at least 15 years of experience in Luxembourg earned up to $119,000 a year,
while teachers in Denmark and Japan with the same level of experience only made salaries of
$54,000 and $65,000 respectively. Meanwhile, Australian and Korean teachers with at least 15
years' experience were paid the lowest salaries, at $48,000 a year. Also worth noting is that it only
took teachers in Australia and Denmark less than 10 years to receive their maximum salary, while
teachers in the other countries had to wait for at least 30 years.

fields.question_text: Closing talk by Dr. Harrison will be held in the ___ Room.
fields.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER.
fields.explanation: The room assigned for the talk is the 'Conference' Room.
fields.passage_excerpt: Dr. Harrison's closing talk has been moved, and it will now be in the Conference Room.
fields.what_question_asks: The specific room for the closing talk.
fields.what_passage_says: The talk is in the Conference Room.
fields.why_answer: 'Conference' identifies the specific room.
fields.paraphrase: held in = will now be in
fields.tip: Watch out for last-minute room changes in the audio.

fields.question_text: Guests must go to the ___ desk to book a time for the steam room.
fields.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER.
fields.explanation: The speaker directs guests to the 'front' desk.
fields.passage_excerpt: If you wish to use the steam room, you need to head over to the front desk to reserve a slot.
fields.what_question_asks: Which desk guests must go to.
fields.what_passage_says: Guests must go to the front desk.
fields.why_answer: 'Front' specifies the desk.
fields.paraphrase: reserve a slot = book a time
fields.tip: Adjectives modifying 'desk' are typical answers.

fields.question_text: To use the steam room, a refundable ___ of £15 is required at reception.
fields.question_instructions: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER.
fields.explanation: The £15 is clearly stated to be a 'deposit'.
fields.passage_excerpt: Please note that a refundable deposit of £15 will be asked for at reception for steam room access.
fields.what_question_asks: What the £15 payment represents.
fields.what_passage_says: The £15 is a deposit.
fields.why_answer: 'Deposit' identifies the type of payment.
fields.paraphrase: is required = will be asked for
fields.tip: Listen for financial terms linked to amounts (e.g., fee, deposit, charge).

fields.question_text: Liam admits he needs to improve his ___.
fields.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
fields.explanation: Liam admits his 'patience' needs improvement.
fields.passage_excerpt: To be honest, the one thing I really need to improve is my patience when working on detailed parts.
fields.what_question_asks: What Liam feels he lacks or needs to improve.
fields.what_passage_says: Liam needs more patience.
fields.why_answer: 'Patience' is what he admits needing to improve.
fields.paraphrase: improve his = work on my
fields.tip: Listen for self-reflective statements.

fields.question_text: Maya struggles with achieving ___ in her sculptures.
fields.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
fields.explanation: Maya states her struggle is achieving 'clarity'.
fields.passage_excerpt: For me, the main struggle is always achieving clarity in the overall message of the sculpture.
fields.what_question_asks: What Maya finds difficult.
fields.what_passage_says: Maya has a hard time achieving clarity.
fields.why_answer: 'Clarity' is the attribute she struggles with.
fields.paraphrase: struggles with = main struggle is
fields.tip: Identify the core noun that follows 'achieving'.

fields.question_text: The ___ will not be available until mid-March.
fields.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
fields.explanation: The speaker mentions the 'foundry' will be unavailable.
fields.passage_excerpt: We have to plan our timeline carefully because the foundry won't be available to us until mid-March.
fields.what_question_asks: What facility or item is unavailable until mid-March.
fields.what_passage_says: The foundry is booked until mid-March.
fields.why_answer: The 'foundry' is the specific place that is unavailable.
fields.paraphrase: not be available = won't be available
fields.tip: Listen for dates or timeframes as anchors.

fields.question_text: Liam chose the seminar on art ___.
fields.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
fields.explanation: Liam selected the seminar on 'conservation'.
fields.passage_excerpt: I eventually decided to choose the seminar focused on art conservation.
fields.what_question_asks: The topic of Liam's chosen seminar.
fields.what_passage_says: Liam picked the conservation seminar.
fields.why_answer: 'Conservation' is the specific topic.
fields.paraphrase: chose = decided to choose
fields.tip: Seminar topics are usually nouns or noun phrases.

fields.question_text: Maya registered for the workshop on designing ___.
fields.question_instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
fields.explanation: Maya registered to learn about designing an 'exhibition'.
fields.passage_excerpt: And I just registered for that interesting workshop on designing an exhibition.
fields.what_question_asks: What Maya's workshop is about designing.
fields.what_passage_says: The workshop is about designing an exhibition.
fields.why_answer: 'Exhibition' fits the blank perfectly.
fields.paraphrase: registered for = signed up for
fields.tip: Listen for 'designing' to find the subsequent noun.
